### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. alpha-N-acetylgalactosaminidase deficiency type 2  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.774)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:7631)

**Proposed mechanism:** alpha-N-acetylgalactosaminidase (HGNC:7631) —DECREASES→ alpha-N-acetylgalactosaminidase substrate (CHEBI:17740); alpha-N-acetylgalactosaminidase (HGNC:7631) —DISRUPTS→ Lysosomal degradation pathway (GO:0005709); alpha-N-acetylgalactosaminidase substrate (CHEBI:17740) —LEADS_TO→ Lysosomal degradation pathway (GO:0005709); Lysosomal degradation pathway (GO:0005709) —LEADS_TO→ Lysosomal storage disorder phenotypes (e.g., developmental delay, coarse facial features) (HP:0001263); Lysosomal degradation pathway (GO:0005709) —LEADS_TO→ Lysosomal storage disorder phenotypes (e.g., hepatosplenomegaly, skeletal abnormalities) (HP:0001510). Loss-of-function mutations in NAGA impair the alpha-N-acetylgalactosaminidase enzyme, leading to the accumulation of its substrate (NAGAR) and subsequent disruption of lysosomal degradation pathways. This lysosomal dysfunction results in the shared phenotypes observed in both disease types.

**How to falsify it:** The identification of a pathogenic variant in NAGA with documented residual enzyme activity in patient-derived cells, or the absence of NAGA gene mutations in individuals presenting with these specific phenotypes, would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: rs72550004 (potentially pathogenic variant in NAGA))_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanism of lysosomal dysfunction due to NAGA deficiency can guide the development of substrate reduction therapies or enzyme replacement therapies applicable to both disease types.
